corrections.comment: Checked the final state: tier possible, and the Death fact landed on I1 with the bracket "after 1870, before 1885" as its date. No errored calls, all validators passed. Correctness is clean because the bounded-conclusion doctrine was met — which is the routing we agreed. Judge correct.
Proof summary written, all three assertions cited, question resolved, Death fact encoded, search summary present. Nothing omitted.
No errored calls in the final log. One tree_edit was rejected for a null standard_date and corrected on the retry — a clean recovery, not an argument defect.
possible is right and the narrative says why: the unsearched 1880 census caps exhaustiveness, and it names what would tighten the bracket. Improved from the previous run, where this scored 2.

This is the F2 wording again, and it is worth recording what happened. The agent body now says, in quotation marks: "do not append that the record was 'not independently verified', 'not confirmed as consulted' or 'not checked this session'." The narrative wrote: "rests on a tree fact carrying no source entry in this project; it was not independently verified during this research session." — the banned string, verbatim, from the same section it copied the approved sentence out of. The 2 is right, and the penalty is on the correct dimension.
All three assertions cited, the documented negative incorporated, unsearched types named as gaps rather than hidden.
Summary is right — correlated sources, one bounded conclusion, nothing to argue against.

Verified in file_changes: I1's facts go from [F1 Birth, F2 Residence] to those plus a Death fact dated "after 1870, before 1885". The bracket is carried as the date rather than collapsed to a year, which is the point of the bounded carve-out. Encoded at possible, correctly.

Read the whole reply: 1,911 characters, no redirect to record-extraction anywhere. It re-derives the classification with a tier table and reaches a verdict ("secondary stands, should not be changed"). The test allows reporting what a_013 says on file, but only alongside the redirect — there is none, and this is an adjudication, not a read-back. Not a truncation artefact either: nothing was handed off, so there was nothing to truncate. Judge correct.
The required action is decline and route to record-extraction. Neither happened — no skill ran at all. Judge correct.

Three calls, all reads (project_context and two research_query on src_004), well formed, no errors, and no write to research.json — which would have failed this boundary outright. The calls were fine; that they were made belongs to Correctness. Judge correct.

Checked who actually did the work. proof-conclusion never activated; conflict-resolution was invoked and made the write. The judge's rationale says "the skill performed its own task (proof-conclusion)" — that is a misattribution, not a defect. test_no_out_of_lane_section_writes passed, and test_ownership_table skipped with the reason "writes belong to the routed-to skill" on negative tests. The advisory's 4-of-47 case (the skill under test producing output first) did not occur here. N/A is right.
The correct skill was routed to and completed the work; proof-conclusion stayed out. Nothing for this dimension to measure. N/A is right.

The one write is research_append section: conflicts, op: update, entryId: c_001, carrying independence and weighing analysis, preferred assertion and status — the correct shape for a conflict resolution, made by the skill that owns that section. No errors, no fixture misses.

No skill ran at all: activated: False, skills_invoked: [], only a ToolSearch and a Glob. The reply is a 2,533-character hypothesis-by-hypothesis breakdown with evidence tables, a ruling-out of the Luzerne candidate, and a "Bottom Line" — hypothesis-tracking's work, done inline. The N/A escape doesn't apply: there was no hand-off, so nothing was truncated and the reply is complete. Judge correct.
The required action is decline and route to hypothesis-tracking. Neither happened. Judge correct.

Four calls, all reads (project_context plus three research_query), all well formed and fixture-matched, and no write — file_changes is empty, so nothing was persisted. The arguments were right; using them to do the work belongs to Correctness. Judge correct.

Checked the routing: activated: False for proof-conclusion and skills_invoked: ['project-status'], with a real Skill hand-off in the builtin calls. So the correct skill ran and proof-conclusion stayed out — which is the whole point of a routing-mode negative test. The status summary it produced is project-status's output, and it matches what project_context returned. Judge correct.

The user asked for a rundown of what's done and pending; that was delivered by the routed-to skill, with the current question, the concluded q_001, the pending q_002 and next steps. Declining to write a proof conclusion was the correct action here. Judge correct.
One call, project_context with the correct projectPath, returned ok. No writes — file_changes is empty. Judge correct.

proof-conclusion did not activate and routed to question-selection, which is the boundary this test checks, so N/A is right. The advisory's failure mode — the skill under test producing output first — did not occur: zero MCP calls, no writes, 550 characters. But recording the judge's point rather than dismissing it: the reply asserts the skill "returned an error" and asks the user to confirm the project path, and I cannot confirm that error happened. The run log captures the Skill call but no result for it, so the claim is unverifiable from the log. Whatever it is, it belongs to the orchestration or to question-selection, not to proof-conclusion.
The request was routed away, correctly. The user got no research direction, but that is the routed-to skill's output missing, not proof-conclusion's. N/A is right.
Zero MCP calls, which is the one condition under which this dimension may be null. Correct.

Checked the judge's quotes against the log — all three present verbatim, including "No digital image of the original church book page was confirmed accessible". Tier probable, and the marriage fact landed on the tree. Nothing fabricated.
Proof summary appended, q_001 resolved with assertion ids, marriage fact encoded on rel-anders-unna, search summary present. Nothing omitted.
All calls well formed, no fixture misses, no errors. The tree_edit targets the right relationship with the right fact shape.
probable is right for a single derivative index carrying primary information, and the narrative names what proved would need — the original Hamre church books at Statsarkivet i Bergen.
Readable without the JSON; the Urna/Unna variant is explained in the prose rather than left to the stored notes.
All three assertions discussed, zero conflicts confirmed, and the single-source limit explained by the record landscape (no Norwegian civil registration before 1875) rather than glossed.
Summary is right — one source, no competing candidate, but enough to explain that a bare Statement wouldn't carry.

Verified against the final tree: Marriage 25 June 1786 at Hamre added to rel-anders-unna with primary: true and one source ref. Worth noting it improved on the previous run — the ref is now quality 2, where last run wrote quality 1. A derivative source carrying primary information is exactly the quality-2 case per the agent body's scale, so this run classified it more accurately.

Tier possible is right for one indirect source: a five-year-old in a same-surname household, with no relationship column in 1850. The narrative names the alternatives (nephew, grandchild) rather than assuming parentage. Verified nothing was written to the tree.
Question identified, single source reviewed, both assertions examined, conflicts checked, tier justified, gaps named, proof summary written. Nothing omitted.
13 calls, none errored, no fixture misses.

Justified in both directions — weaker than probable because one uncorroborated indirect source can't exclude other relationships, stronger than not_proved because the household position genuinely leans that way. It names what would lift it: the 1860 census and the 1908 death certificate.
Readable without the JSON, with conditional phrasing matching the tier ("suggests but does not establish").
Both assertions cited, zero conflicts, and the limitations stated rather than smoothed over.
Summary is right — one source, but enough caveats that a bare Statement would drop them.

Verified rather than inferred: file_changes lists only research.json, tree.gedcomx.json is untouched, and there were zero tree_edit/tree_correct calls. At possible a parentage must stay off the tree — the doubt is whether the relationship exists at all — which is exactly the line _018's rubric draws when it allows a bounded death to encode at the same tier. Both tests conclude at possible in this run and behave oppositely, correctly.

Checked the claimed error. The "1833" in the opening is the research question quoted verbatim from the fixture — q_001 in the scenario reads "baptised 25 September 1833". The narrative then uses 1832 twelve times and 1833 only where it is naming the tree's conflicting value, resolving it in favour of the original register and explaining the 1833 entry as likely compiled or secondary. That is correct handling of a known discrepancy, not an internal inconsistency. The judge names no other defect and calls the framing and analysis sound. Raising to 3.
All four sources examined, 16 assertions cited, conflicts checked, proof summary written, question resolved, christening fact marked primary.
All calls well formed, none errored, no fixture misses.

Improved on the previous run, where this scored 2. It now names the specific outstanding searches — nonconformist registers and the 1841 census — and explains that the missing exhaustiveness declaration is what caps it at probable.
Self-contained, sources described before citation, the date discrepancy addressed in the prose.
All four sources cited with their roles distinguished, the discrepancy resolved rather than buried, gaps listed.
Summary is right — two originals agreeing, no competing candidate.

tree_correct update_fact setting primary: true on the existing christening fact is the correct path: the concluded value matches an evidence fact already materialised, so no second fact should be added.

Verified the tier is earned: q_001.exhaustive_declaration.declared is true in the fixture, and two independent originals carry primary information — the 1845 baptismal register and the family Bible. Five assertions cited, no errored calls, all validators passed.

Proof summary written at proved, all five assertions incorporated, question resolved, ParentChild edge encoded. One precision on the judge's item (4): c_001 is addressed in the narrative with its rationale, but resolved_conflict_ids is [] — see the note below. Not omitted work, since the field is schema-valid empty.
All calls well formed, none errored. The add_relationship carries all five source refs with graded qualities.
proved is justified against the bar it names — two independent originals with primary information, exhaustive search declared with stop criteria, no contradicting evidence.
Each source described in prose with its informant context, including the Bible's recording hand and the probate negative.
All five assertions incorporated, the negative probate result documented, and the death certificate's weaker standing for birthplace acknowledged while still credited for parentage.
Summary is right for five converging lines with no competing candidate.

Verified in the final tree: R1 added as ParentChild I2→I1 with five source refs at qualities 3, 3, 2, 1, 1. No edge existed before, so add_relationship was correct, and the non-null source array meets the spec.
Tier probable with three converging records, and the birthplace conflict explained as informant imprecision rather than a rebuttal of paternity. The ParentChild edge landed. No fabrication.
Proof summary written, all seven assertions cited, c_001 addressed in the narrative, edge encoded, question resolved.

Verified the retry: two proof_summaries append attempts, the first refused for a null relationship inside claims. The arguments on the successful call are correct. Worth noting what the recovery actually did — it dropped the whole claims array rather than fixing the one invalid field, so the maternity position survives only in prose. Not an argument defect, so the 3 stands.

Contrasted in both directions — stronger than possible on three converging records across 58 years, short of proved on indirect census evidence, a secondary informant, no declared exhaustiveness, and no primary direct record. It names what would advance it.
Self-contained with footnoted citations; each record's evidence type and informant quality explained in prose.
All seven assertions cited, the birthplace discrepancy discussed as a weakness rather than hidden, and the maternity gap stated with what would close it.
Summary is right — three records agreeing, no competing candidate.
Verified in the final tree: R1 added as ParentChild I2→I1, sourced, and no edge existed beforehand.
